subject: Spend ambit validation — next steps & procurement thresholds
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@orchard.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spend ambit validation — next steps & procurement thresholds

Hi Samir — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can get you a formal quote and align on procurement timing: 

Recap (from our call)
- Expected pilot monthly consumption: ~50M — 150M tokens (spikes possible; mostly batch generation).
- Target unit economics discussed: target ~$450 per 1M tokens for pilot usage; open to commit discounts.
- Budget aperture: roughly $22k — $68k / month at the target rate for expected volume.
- Procurement gate: your team indicated a PO is required for any monthly spend > $50k. If the monthly spend is below that, an invoice + CC/net term is preferred.

Attachments included: redwood_pricing_estimate_20280719.xlsx (pricing scenarios across volumes / reserved vs on-demand).

Proposed next steps
1) Please confirm the procurement threshold (you mentioned PO > $50k today — is that a hard floor or negotiable with legal?).
2) If PO required, please share the contact at procurement and any template (we can pre-fill).
3) If you want a lower unit cost we can model a 6-month reserved capacity commitment; I included a worked example in the attached spreadsheet.
4) Can we schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to finalize the quote and timing? I’m available Tue/Wed afternoon PT.

If any of the recap items above are incorrect, flag them and I’ll update. Happy to jump on a quick call to resolve procurement questions.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spend ambit validation — next steps & procurement thresholds

Thanks Naomi — good summary. A couple clarifications from my side: 

- Procurement threshold: our standard policy is PO required for monthly committed spend >= $40k. I misstated on the call — apologies. For one-off spikes we can approve exceptions but anything expected to be recurring at scale will need a PO.
- We do need a formal quote + SOW for our purchasing process (legal requires scope + pricing). Could you attach a one-page SOW and a PDF quote?
- Procurement contact is procurement@orchard.ai (copied). I attached our PO template for reference.

Would like to keep the pilot flexible (50–150M) but with a hard cap for billing during the pilot; procurement wants to see the upper-bound cost. Your workbook will help.

Happy to take the follow-up meeting next Tue 10:00 PT if that works for you.

Best,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product — Orchard AI
samir@orchard.ai

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@orchard.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, procurement@orchard.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2028 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spend ambit validation — next steps & procurement thresholds

Perfect — thanks for the clarification on the PO floor. Quick answers and options so we can align with your procurement workflow: 

1) Quote & SOW: I’ll produce a one-page SOW and a formal PDF quote that shows three scenarios (on-demand, 6-month reserved, and capped-pilot pricing). I’ll attach both in my follow-up.
2) PO threshold: because your internal policy is PO required >= $40k, we can map our billing flow accordingly. Operationally we see two practical paths:
   a) Pilot on on-demand billing with an upper monthly cap (your PO not required if < $40k), or
   b) Commit to a 6-month reserved pool which lowers unit cost (~$380 per 1M tokens in the worked example) and then a PO can be issued for the committed amount (this brings predictability for both sides).
3) Net terms: Redwood typically offers Net30 once the PO is in place; we can discuss Net45 for enterprise procurement if necessary.

Proposed next actions: I’ll send the PDF quote + SOW by EOD Monday and we can take the Tue 10:00 PT slot to walk through the SOW with procurement (procurement@orchard.ai). If procurement needs redlines, loop in legal during that session and we’ll include our standard SLAs.

Thanks — attaching the pricing workbook we discussed and noting the cell with the reserve-commit example for quick reference.

Naomi
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_pricing_estimate_20280719.xlsx (pricing workbook, highlighted reserved example)

Date: Sat, 20 Jul 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spend ambit validation — next steps & procurement thresholds

Looping in a quick legal/ops note — Naomi, excellent recap. Two things for planning: 

- Legal lead time: for PO-based deals we typically see 10–14 business days from receipt of a standard SOW + procurement form to signature for mid-market customers. If Orchard needs faster turnaround, we should surface any non-standard T&Cs up front.
- Billing trigger: confirm whether Orchard prefers monthly invoicing against committed pool or monthly reconciliation (invoice for actual consumption with reserves credited). That affects finance lead time and how we should structure the quote.

Samir — I’ve added a very short SOW template that Naomi can use as the base (I’ll drop the file into the Drive link she already referenced). Naomi — please include the pricing table variant that maps to a $40k PO threshold and the 6-month reserved commitment in the PDF.

-Markus
